## Diameter stress, boundary flux, and exact unit contacts

28 October 2026 · Independent mathematical assessment · No repository modifications

Verdict: The boundary-flux approach yields rigorous, all-label restrictions on equilibrium stresses, but does not yet force an exact unit equilateral triangle in a global diameter minimizer.

The main findings are:

1. Every global minimizer admits a normalized nonnegative equilibrium stress on its original unit contacts and diametral pairs. This gives an exact vector cut-flux identity and a universal weighted flux bound.
2. Only O(D)O(D)O(D) original sites can be endpoints of diameter constraints. Thus almost all original sites satisfy contact-only equilibrium equations, although their contact multipliers may all vanish.
3. Triangle-free rhombic grids can transport balanced stress through their interior without producing unit triangles.
4. Positive semidefinite equilibrium stress, even combined with a nearly circular hull, is not a global-optimality certificate.
5. The missing implication is a quantitative, endpoint-sensitive restriction on how diameter stress must enter the original interior contact network.

This remains a structural investigation, not a proof or disproof of [Erdős Problem #99](https://www.erdosproblems.com/99?utm_source=chatgpt.com). The problem asks about every sufficiently large global minimizer, rather than every stationary, rigid, densely packed, or asymptotically optimal configuration. Erdos Problems+1

## 1. Exact equilibrium for all original labels

Let P=(p1,…,pn)⊂R2P=(p_1,\ldots,p_n)\subset\mathbb R^2P=(p1​,…,pn​)⊂R2 be a global minimizer, with

∣pi−pj∣≥1,D=max⁡i<j∣pi−pj∣.|p_i-p_j|\geq1,\qquad D=\max_{i<j}|p_i-p_j|.∣pi​−pj​∣≥1,D=i<jmax​∣pi​−pj​∣.

Define the complete active sets

C={ij:∣pi−pj∣=1},H={ij:∣pi−pj∣=D}.C=\{ij:|p_i-p_j|=1\}, \qquad H=\{ij:|p_i-p_j|=D\}.C={ij:∣pi​−pj​∣=1},H={ij:∣pi​−pj​∣=D}.

No original point is discarded, including contact isolates and vertices receiving zero stress.

Theorem 1 — Normalized equilibrium and stress tensor.

There exist multipliers αe≥0\alpha_e\geq0αe​≥0 for e∈Ce\in Ce∈C and βh≥0\beta_h\geq0βh​≥0 for h∈Hh\in Hh∈H such that

∑h∈Hβh=1(1)\boxed{\sum_{h\in H}\beta_h=1} \tag{1}h∈H∑​βh​=1​(1)

and, at every original label iii,

∑j:ij∈Cαij(pi−pj)=∑j:ij∈Hβij(pi−pj).(2)\boxed{ \sum_{j:ij\in C}\alpha_{ij}(p_i-p_j) = \sum_{j:ij\in H}\beta_{ij}(p_i-p_j). } \tag{2}j:ij∈C∑​αij​(pi​−pj​)=j:ij∈H∑​βij​(pi​−pj​).​(2)

Furthermore,

∑e∈Cαe=D2(3)\boxed{\sum_{e\in C}\alpha_e=D^2} \tag{3}e∈C∑​αe​=D2​(3)

and the following matrix equality holds exactly:

∑ij∈Cαij(pi−pj)(pi−pj)T=∑ij∈Hβij(pi−pj)(pi−pj)T.(4)\boxed{ \sum_{ij\in C}\alpha_{ij} (p_i-p_j)(p_i-p_j)^{\mathsf T} = \sum_{ij\in H}\beta_{ij} (p_i-p_j)(p_i-p_j)^{\mathsf T}. } \tag{4}ij∈C∑​αij​(pi​−pj​)(pi​−pj​)T=ij∈H∑​βij​(pi​−pj​)(pi​−pj​)T.​(4)

### Proof

Introduce t=D2t=D^2t=D2 as an optimization variable. Minimize ttt subject to

1−∣pi−pj∣2≤0,∣pi−pj∣2−t≤01-|p_i-p_j|^2\leq0, \qquad |p_i-p_j|^2-t\leq01−∣pi​−pj​∣2≤0,∣pi​−pj​∣2−t≤0

for all distinct pairs.

The Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification holds. Indeed, choose an infinitesimal velocity p˙i=pi\dot p_i=p_ip˙​i​=pi​ and t˙=2t+1\dot t=2t+1t˙=2t+1. Every active separation inequality has derivative −2-2−2, while every active upper-distance inequality has derivative −1-1−1. Hence there is a direction strictly decreasing all active constraint functions.

The Lagrangian is

L=t+∑ij∈Cαij(1−∣pi−pj∣2)+∑ij∈Hβij(∣pi−pj∣2−t).\mathcal L=t+ \sum_{ij\in C}\alpha_{ij} (1-|p_i-p_j|^2) + \sum_{ij\in H}\beta_{ij} (|p_i-p_j|^2-t).L=t+ij∈C∑​αij​(1−∣pi​−pj​∣2)+ij∈H∑​βij​(∣pi​−pj​∣2−t).

Stationarity with respect to ttt gives (1), and stationarity with respect to every pip_ipi​ gives (2).

Multiplying (2) by pip_ipi​, summing over all labels, and combining the two ends of each edge yields

∑Cαe∣e∣2=∑Hβh∣h∣2.\sum_C\alpha_e |e|^2 = \sum_H\beta_h |h|^2.C∑​αe​∣e∣2=H∑​βh​∣h∣2.

The active lengths are exactly 111 and DDD, proving (3). Repeating the calculation with the two coordinate components separately gives the matrix identity (4).

All these are necessary conditions for genuine global minimizers. They are not sufficient conditions. □\square□

This stress framework is also developed in Archit Das, Stress, rigidity and rhombic reductions for an Erdős minimum-diameter problem (15 September 2026), [Zenodo preprint](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22768362?utm_source=chatgpt.com). The derivation above is independent of that work. Zenodo

## 2. Boundary flux: an unconditional all-label theorem

For any set WWW of original labels, let δC(W)\delta_C(W)δC​(W) be the unit-contact edges with exactly one endpoint in WWW, and define δH(W)\delta_H(W)δH​(W) similarly.

Summing (2) over WWW cancels every internal edge.

Theorem 2 — Exact vector cut equilibrium.

For any W⊆{1,…,n}W\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}W⊆{1,…,n},

∑ij∈δC(W)i∈Wαij(pi−pj)=∑ij∈δH(W)i∈Wβij(pi−pj).(5)\boxed{ \sum_{\substack{ij\in\delta_C(W)\\i\in W}} \alpha_{ij}(p_i-p_j) = \sum_{\substack{ij\in\delta_H(W)\\i\in W}} \beta_{ij}(p_i-p_j). } \tag{5}ij∈δC​(W)i∈W​∑​αij​(pi​−pj​)=ij∈δH​(W)i∈W​∑​βij​(pi​−pj​).​(5)

This holds for disconnected, irregular, multiply connected, or completely inactive subsets WWW.

For a unit vector ν\nuν and real threshold sss, take the half-plane cut

Ws={i:ν⋅pi≤s}.W_s=\{i:\nu\cdot p_i\leq s\}.Ws​={i:ν⋅pi​≤s}.

Every edge crossing this cut points toward increasing ν\nuν-coordinate when oriented from WsW_sWs​ to its complement. Projecting (5) onto ν\nuν consequently gives

∑ij∈δC(Ws)αij∣ν⋅(pi−pj)∣=∑ij∈δH(Ws)βij∣ν⋅(pi−pj)∣≤D.(6)\boxed{ \sum_{ij\in\delta_C(W_s)} \alpha_{ij}|\nu\cdot(p_i-p_j)| = \sum_{ij\in\delta_H(W_s)} \beta_{ij}|\nu\cdot(p_i-p_j)| \leq D. } \tag{6}ij∈δC​(Ws​)∑​αij​∣ν⋅(pi​−pj​)∣=ij∈δH​(Ws​)∑​βij​∣ν⋅(pi​−pj​)∣≤D.​(6)

The last inequality follows from ∣pi−pj∣=D|p_i-p_j|=D∣pi​−pj​∣=D on HHH and ∑Hβh=1\sum_H\beta_h=1∑H​βh​=1.

This is an exact weighted boundary-flux bound in every direction, at every threshold. There is no asymptotic error, generic-position assumption, or deletion of labels.

### Two useful consequences

Corollary 2.1 — Diameter loading is confined to O(D)O(D)O(D) labels.

Every diameter endpoint is an exposed vertex of the convex hull K=conv⁡PK=\operatorname{conv}PK=convP: the vector joining a diameter pair defines opposite supporting lines, each touching the configuration only at the corresponding endpoint.

For a nondegenerate hull, consecutive hull vertices have distance at least one. Thus the number hhh of hull vertices obeys

h≤per⁡(K)≤πD.(7)h\leq \operatorname{per}(K)\leq\pi D. \tag{7}h≤per(K)≤πD.(7)

The second inequality follows from Cauchy's perimeter formula and the bound DDD on every width.

Therefore at most πD\pi DπD original sites are incident to any diameter pair. All other original sites satisfy the homogeneous contact-equilibrium equation

∑j:ij∈Cαij(pi−pj)=0.(8)\sum_{j:ij\in C}\alpha_{ij}(p_i-p_j)=0. \tag{8}j:ij∈C∑​αij​(pi​−pj​)=0.(8)

Corollary 2.2 — Positive boundary contacts require diameter loading.

Suppose pip_ipi​ is a convex-hull vertex with no incident positive diameter multiplier. Choose a supporting normal ν\nuν strictly exposing that vertex.

Taking the scalar product of (2) with ν\nuν, the right-hand side is zero, while every term on the left is nonnegative and is strictly positive whenever its multiplier is positive. Consequently,

αij=0for every unit contact ij incident to i.(9)\boxed{\alpha_{ij}=0\quad\text{for every unit contact }ij\text{ incident to }i.} \tag{9}αij​=0for every unit contact ij incident to i.​(9)

Hence every hull vertex carrying a positive contact multiplier must also carry a positive diameter multiplier.

Both corollaries are independent of the triangle-free assumption.

### What the flux bound does not say

Equation (6) controls the weighted projection of crossing contacts. It does not imply

∣δC(Ws)∣≤D,|\delta_C(W_s)|\leq D,∣δC​(Ws​)∣≤D,

nor does it yield a positive lower bound on any αe\alpha_eαe​.

An original edge with αe=0\alpha_e=0αe​=0 is still an exact unit contact. Conversely, a site with six geometrically near-hexagonal neighbors may have no exact unit contacts at all.

Thus converting (6) into an unweighted contact-count obstruction requires additional, genuinely global information.

## 3. Diameter-free patches and stress conservation

The flux identity has a useful localized consequence that does not require convexity.

Theorem 3 — Interior stress must be supplied through its boundary.

Let WWW be any collection of original sites with no incident positive diameter multiplier. For a point z∈conv⁡{pi:i∈W}z\in\operatorname{conv}\{p_i:i\in W\}z∈conv{pi​:i∈W}, write dW=diam⁡{pi:i∈W}d_W=\operatorname{diam}\{p_i:i\in W\}dW​=diam{pi​:i∈W}.

Then

∑ij∈Ci,j∈Wαij≤dW∑ij∈δC(W)αij.(10)\boxed{ \sum_{\substack{ij\in C\\i,j\in W}}\alpha_{ij} \leq d_W\sum_{ij\in\delta_C(W)}\alpha_{ij}. } \tag{10}ij∈Ci,j∈W​∑​αij​≤dW​ij∈δC​(W)∑​αij​.​(10)

### Proof

Use the test velocity

vi={pi−z,i∈W,0,i∉W.v_i= \begin{cases} p_i-z,&i\in W,\\ 0,&i\notin W. \end{cases}vi​={pi​−z,0,​i∈W,i∈/W.​

Taking the scalar product of the full equilibrium system (2) with these velocities and summing over the original labels gives

0=∑ij∈Ci,j∈Wαij+∑ij∈δC(W)i∈Wαij(pi−pj)⋅(pi−z).0= \sum_{\substack{ij\in C\\i,j\in W}}\alpha_{ij} + \sum_{\substack{ij\in\delta_C(W)\\i\in W}} \alpha_{ij}(p_i-p_j)\cdot(p_i-z).0=ij∈Ci,j∈W​∑​αij​+ij∈δC​(W)i∈W​∑​αij​(pi​−pj​)⋅(pi​−z).

Here every diameter term vanishes because no positive diameter edge is incident to WWW.

Since contact edges have length one and ∣pi−z∣≤dW|p_i-z|\leq d_W∣pi​−z∣≤dW​, taking absolute values of the boundary sum proves (10). □\square□

In particular, a connected component of the positive-contact stress graph that has no positive diameter loading cannot exist: taking WWW to be that component makes its positive crossing-contact flux zero, forcing all its internal multipliers to vanish.

This gives a precise transport interpretation:

Every positive interior stress component must ultimately connect to the diameter-loaded boundary.

However, an original geometric contact component need not be a positive-stress component. Its edges can all have zero multiplier. The theorem therefore constrains the stressed network, not the complete original contact graph.

## 4. Test against triangle-free rhombic grids

Take two unit vectors

u=(1,0),v=(cos⁡θ,sin⁡θ),π3<θ<π2,u=(1,0),\qquad v=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta), \qquad \frac{\pi}{3}<\theta<\frac{\pi}{2},u=(1,0),v=(cosθ,sinθ),3π​<θ<2π​,

and the lattice

Λθ={iu+jv:i,j∈Z}.\Lambda_\theta=\{iu+jv:i,j\in\mathbb Z\}.Λθ​={iu+jv:i,j∈Z}.

### Exact separation and absence of unit triangles

For any lattice displacement,

∣iu+jv∣2=i2+j2+2ijcos⁡θ.|iu+jv|^2=i^2+j^2+2ij\cos\theta.∣iu+jv∣2=i2+j2+2ijcosθ.

If ij<0ij<0ij<0, putting a=∣i∣a=|i|a=∣i∣, b=∣j∣b=|j|b=∣j∣ gives

∣iu+jv∣2=a2+b2−2abcos⁡θ>a2+b2−ab≥1.|iu+jv|^2 =a^2+b^2-2ab\cos\theta >a^2+b^2-ab\geq1.∣iu+jv∣2=a2+b2−2abcosθ>a2+b2−ab≥1.

### Exact interior stress conservation

Let aija_{ij}aij​ be the multiplier on the horizontal grid edge from (i,j)(i,j)(i,j) to (i+1,j)(i+1,j)(i+1,j), and bijb_{ij}bij​ its vertical counterpart.

At an interior site with four grid contacts and no diameter loading, (8) becomes

(ai−1,j−aij)u+(bi,j−1−bij)v=0.(a_{i-1,j}-a_{ij})u+ (b_{i,j-1}-b_{ij})v=0.(ai−1,j​−aij​)u+(bi,j−1​−bij​)v=0.

Because uuu and vvv are linearly independent,

ai−1,j=aij,bi,j−1=bij.(11)\boxed{ a_{i-1,j}=a_{ij},\qquad b_{i,j-1}=b_{ij}. } \tag{11}ai−1,j​=aij​,bi,j−1​=bij​.​(11)

Positive horizontal stress is constant along each uninterrupted row; vertical stress is constant along each uninterrupted column.

This is an exact discrete conservation law. There is no local triangle contradiction: the four positive forces can balance perfectly.

### Near-circular, almost densest rhombic crops

For an additional geometric check, take

PR=ΛθR∩B(0,R),θR=π3+1R.P_R=\Lambda_{\theta_R}\cap B(0,R), \qquad \theta_R=\frac{\pi}{3}+\frac1R.PR​=ΛθR​​∩B(0,R),θR​=3π​+R1​.

A fundamental parallelogram has area sin⁡θR\sin\theta_RsinθR​ and diameter at most two. The elementary lattice-cell argument therefore gives

∣PR∣=πR2sin⁡θR+O(R)=πR23/2+O(R).|P_R|=\frac{\pi R^2}{\sin\theta_R}+O(R) =\frac{\pi R^2}{\sqrt3/2}+O(R).∣PR​∣=sinθR​πR2​+O(R)=3​/2πR2​+O(R).

The same covering argument shows

B(0,R−4)⊆conv⁡PR⊆B(0,R).B(0,R-4)\subseteq\operatorname{conv}P_R \subseteq B(0,R).B(0,R−4)⊆convPR​⊆B(0,R).

Consequently the actual diameter is 2R+O(1)2R+O(1)2R+O(1), the hull's isodiametric area deficit is O(R)O(R)O(R), and the configuration has asymptotically optimal leading-order density—yet contains no unit equilateral triple.

These are feasible crops, not certified diameter minimizers or necessarily KKT-stationary configurations.

The result identifies the limitation of any proposal based solely on asymptotic density, near-circularity, and local balanced rhombic contacts. Endpoint optimality must rule out these models by an additional argument.

## 5. Strong countermodel: near-circular, dense, PSD-stressed, but nonglobal

The next construction simultaneously tests most of the proposed hypotheses. It retains every original label.

Proposition 4 — An asymptotically dense triangle-free family with exact KKT equilibrium and PSD stress.

There are arbitrarily large configurations PmP_mPm​, with diameters Dm→∞D_m\to\inftyDm​→∞, satisfying all of the following:

min⁡i≠j∣pi−pj∣=1,nm=πDm223+O(Dm),πDm24−area⁡(conv⁡Pm)⟶π6,per⁡(conv⁡Pm)=πDm+o(1).(12)\begin{gathered} \min_{i\ne j}|p_i-p_j|=1,\\ n_m=\frac{\pi D_m^2}{2\sqrt3}+O(D_m),\\ \frac{\pi D_m^2}{4} -\operatorname{area}(\operatorname{conv}P_m) \longrightarrow\frac{\pi}{6},\\ \operatorname{per}(\operatorname{conv}P_m) =\pi D_m+o(1). \end{gathered} \tag{12}i=jmin​∣pi​−pj​∣=1,nm​=23​πDm2​​+O(Dm​),4πDm2​​−area(convPm​)⟶6π​,per(convPm​)=πDm​+o(1).​(12)

They have no unit triangles, admit exact normalized nonnegative KKT multipliers, and their complete original-label stress matrices are positive semidefinite. Nevertheless, every sufficiently large member has a strictly smaller-diameter competitor with the same number of sites.

qj=R(cos⁡(2πj/m),sin⁡(2πj/m)),j=0,…,m−1.q_j=R(\cos(2\pi j/m),\sin(2\pi j/m)), \qquad j=0,\ldots,m-1.qj​=R(cos(2πj/m),sin(2πj/m)),j=0,…,m−1.

The interior contact graph is a square grid, and the exterior contact graph is an mmm-cycle. Neither has triangles. Hence the entire original configuration is triangle-free.

The only diametral pairs are the m/2m/2m/2 opposite pairs of boundary vertices. In particular, none of the dense interior labels participates in a diameter constraint.

### Exact equilibrium and PSD certificate

Assign to every boundary contact the multiplier

α=1msin⁡2ϕ,\alpha=\frac{1}{m\sin^2\phi},α=msin2ϕ1​,

β=2m.\beta=\frac2m.β=m2​.

(qj−qj−1)+(qj−qj+1)=4sin⁡2ϕqj,(q_j-q_{j-1})+(q_j-q_{j+1}) =4\sin^2\phi\,q_j,(qj​−qj−1​)+(qj​−qj+1​)=4sin2ϕqj​,

### Referee interpretation

This is a strong negative test for the proposed stress-flux mechanism:

Near-circular hull + asymptotically optimal population + exact all-label KKT + PSD stress + isotropic diameter stress does not imply a unit triangle.

The configuration fails actual global optimality. It also fails the unconditional sharper population requirement for an optimizer at its own diameter. That is precisely why it cannot settle Erdős #99.

The example shows that global optimality must do substantive work; it cannot be replaced by those necessary conditions.

## 6. Stronger countermodel: full positive stress, PSD matrix, and mixed rigidity

The natural strategy suggested by the calculations is to treat the diameter-loaded hull as a source of normalized force and ask how much of that force must penetrate the original packing.

The zero-vacancy obstruction is real, but it does not prevent all same-nnn diameter improvements. In particular, I obtain three rigorous conclusions:

1. There are arbitrarily large, exactly unit-separated, triangle-free two-grain configurations whose entire convex hull is saturated: no additional unit-separated site can be inserted anywhere inside it.

## 8. Additional exact graph restrictions — useful, but insufficient

Two elementary consequences are worth recording because they operate on original sites and exact contacts, not approximate neighbors.

### Exact contact degree at most five in a triangle-free packing

Around a site pip_ipi​, unit-contact neighbors lie on the unit circle. Consecutive contact directions have angular separation at least 60∘60^\circ60∘, since their endpoints must be at least unit separated.

If six unit-contact neighbors existed, all six angular gaps would equal 60∘60^\circ60∘. Each adjacent pair would then be at distance exactly 111, producing a unit equilateral triangle with pip_ipi​.

Therefore

triangle-free⟹deg⁡C(pi)≤5.(25)\boxed{ \text{triangle-free}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \deg_C(p_i)\le5. } \tag{25}triangle-free⟹degC​(pi​)≤5.​(25)

### Triangle-free contact graphs have at most 2n−42n-42n−4 edges

Unit-contact segments cannot cross properly. If two such segments crossed, choosing an endpoint on the shorter half of each segment would give two original sites at mutual distance strictly less than 111.

Thus the original unit-contact graph is a planar straight-line graph. If it is triangle-free, Euler's planar edge inequality gives

∣C∣≤2n−4(n≥3).(26)\boxed{|C|\le2n-4\qquad(n\ge3).} \tag{26}∣C∣≤2n−4(n≥3).​(26)

Neither conclusion follows from KKT. The regular-polygon stationary family has only nnn unit contacts, while the globally optimal six-point configuration has only five.

Likewise, having six near-unit neighbors is not equivalent to having six exactly unit neighbors.

## 8. Exact inference gaps and research priorities

The results distinguish three questions.

First, whether Dn=Dn+1D_n=D_{n+1}Dn​=Dn+1​ for some large nnn is a global cardinality question. Compactness gives an exact insertion characterization, but the Oler/lattice bounds do not decide individual plateaus.

pn<1.650n−1p_n<1.650\sqrt{n-1}pn​<1.650n−1​

prevents long plateaus but permits isolated or shorter plateaus at arbitrarily large cardinalities. No assertion of eventual strict monotonicity follows.

Third, even if eventual strict monotonicity were proved, it would not settle the existence of exact unit equilateral triangles. The square already demonstrates why such an implication requires an additional theorem.

The strongest candidate deductions that survive audit are the global bound (Theorem 3), the deletion constraints (Theorem 4), and conditional triangle-transversal rigidity (Theorem 5).

### Recommended priorities

1. Classify or exclude large-nnn plateaus using global rigidity. A useful sufficient theorem would say that no globally optimal nnn-site configuration admits an additional feasible site at diameter DnD_nDn​. It must quantify over all globally optimal nnn-configurations, not one chosen packing.

2. Investigate active-constraint certificates. For a proposed plateau of length kkk, every globally optimal (n+k)(n+k)(n+k)-configuration must have unit-contact and diameter graphs with vertex-cover number at least k+1k+1k+1. These are exact combinatorial necessary conditions that could be combined with independent geometric restrictions.

3. Seek quantitative improvements to the global slack identity (4). Any universal improvement to o(D)o(D)o(D) plateau length would need a new lower bound on the combined deficit terms, or an argument not captured by Oler's inequality. Such an improvement alone would still be insufficient for Erdős 99.

4. Keep the triangle condition as a separate endpoint certification problem. ## 1. Verdict

The six-near-neighbor hypothesis does not, by itself, force an exact unit triangle, even when almost every vertex has a nearly perfect hexagonal neighborhood.

There is a particularly strong obstruction: an arbitrarily small deformation of a triangular lattice can retain four exact unit contacts and six near-unit neighbors at every bulk vertex while eliminating every exact unit triangle.

The graph-theoretic analysis gives three rigorous conclusions:

1. A planar unit-separated configuration without unit triangles has a unit-contact graph with at most 2n−42n-42n−4 edges and maximum degree at most five.
2. In a nearly triangular plane triangulation, avoiding unit triangles forces a positive proportion of the triangulation edges to have length strictly greater than one. It does not force a positive total length excess.
3. Such triangle-free contact graphs are infinitesimally flexible as bar frameworks, but this does not imply that the configuration's diameter can be reduced while preserving separation.

Consequently, Euler's formula, local kissing-number arguments, near-hexagonal degree counts, and ordinary bar rigidity do not resolve the global endpoint problem.

The conclusion remains consistent with the official statement, which is listed as open. Erdős Problems

## 7. Exact inference gaps and research priorities

The results isolate three different obstacles.

First, near-hexagonal local geometry says that most sites have six neighbors at distances 1+o(1)1+o(1)1+o(1), but it does not make those distances exactly one. Likewise, the universal stress-support theorem produces a component spanning nearly the full diameter without proving that it occupies positive area or contains a cycle, much less a unit triangle.

Second, a global-optimal representative with numerous exact contacts is not enough for Erdős #99. The conjecture quantifies over every optimizer. The n=8n=8n=8 family demonstrates that the same global diameter can support substantially different exact-contact graphs.

Third, active-contact abundance does not imply positive KKT multipliers. Complementary slackness is one-way; the n=8n=8n=8 center provides an exact example of contacts with zero multiplier.

The most useful next priorities, in order, are:

1. Upgrade stress support from diameter-spanning to area-filling. Seek an endpoint theorem proving that every normalized KKT stress has positive-contact support on n−O(D)n-O(D)n−O(D) originals, or otherwise prove that a large unweighted component forces a strict global diameter improvement. Theorem 2 provides an unconditional starting bound but not the needed upgrade.
2. Study exact flexes of unweighted originals. In particular, determine when a positive-contact component spanning 3D/2\sqrt3D/23​D/2 can coexist with a large locally near-hexagonal but entirely zero-stress region. First-order equilibrium alone is unlikely to eliminate such regions.
3. Combine contact-richness with triangle-free preservation. Theorems 3 and 4 separately supply degree-two richness and triangle-free-safe degree-one saturation. An exact deformation argument delivering both, without relaxing global optimality, would be more directly relevant.
4. Exploit original angular hull vertices as boundary anchors. The sector theorem supplies many authentic extreme sites in each fixed direction, but a further exact mechanical linkage is needed to transmit their diameter constraints into unit-contact stress in the bulk.

## 7. The remaining inference gap

The exact endpoint identity (1) is potentially useful because it replaces an approximate packing statement with a finite system of equality constraints on the original labels.

It supplies a necessary equilibrium between all unit contacts and diametral pairs, and its affine projection (3) gives a particularly inexpensive disqualification test for proposed optimizers.

A sufficient combinatorial route would be to prove that every sufficiently large global optimizer has more than 2n−42n-42n−4 unit-contact edges. The unit-contact graph is planar, and a triangle-free planar graph has at most 2n−42n-42n−4 edges. But the required contact-count inequality is not established by the present stress theorem, Oler's inequality, or the angular hull-vertex distribution.

The other possible route would be to show that a triangle-free global optimizer necessarily admits a strictly improving first-order motion of the kind ruled out in Theorem 2. At present, no such universal motion is proved: triangle-free contact systems may possess balanced positive stresses.

## 7. The missing exact endpoint-rigidity lemma

The strongest plausible next step is not another density estimate but a global exclusion of quadrilateral-supported optimizers.

One sufficient theorem would be:

> For every sufficiently large nnn, if an nnn-point unit-separated configuration has globally minimum diameter and no unit equilateral triangle, then there is a feasible deformation of all original labels, retaining their pairwise separation, that strictly decreases the diameter.

This would solve the problem directly. The present results do not establish such a deformation.

The key difficulties are that the diameter is a maximum over all pairs, unit contacts may form rigid-looking rhombic networks, some labels may be unstressed, and the boundary diametral constraints can obstruct a global shear even when local square-grid-type contacts allow one.

The September 2026 Das preprint describes a related residual obstruction as boundary pinning of rhombic train-track rotations. Its stated reduction to 2n−O(n)2n-O(\sqrt n)2n−O(n​) contacts when the stress support is large stops on the non-forcing side of the threshold. Zenodo

An exact strict-improvement proof would need to control all active diameter pairs and all unit contacts simultaneously, or furnish a separate global comparison against every same-nnn packing. Infinitesimal flexibility without a feasible finite deformation is insufficient.

## 6. Referee assessment of stronger nonlinear approaches

The examples above identify precise failure modes.

| Proposed criterion | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| KKT stationarity with nonnegative stress | Necessary, insufficient; fails already at n=6,8n=6,8n=6,8 |
| Positive-semidefinite primary stress | Sufficient for global optimality, not necessary |
| Positive stress on every original site | Not necessary; the eight-point center is unstressed |
| Second-order necessary optimality conditions | Cannot by themselves force triangles for large nnn |
| All-orders local diameter minimality | Insufficient by Theorem 4 |
| Global infeasibility certificate (1) | Necessary and sufficient for fixed-candidate global optimality |
| Global triangle-free exclusion certificate (3) | Necessary and sufficient for the fixed-nnn Erdős conclusion |

There is a more precise way to describe the limitation of perturbative methods. The contact and diameter constraints are quadratic polynomials. Along any perturbative curve

x(t)=x+tv+t2w+⋯,x(t)=x+tv+t^2w+\cdots,x(t)=x+tv+t2w+⋯,

the feasibility conditions must hold at their first nonzero coefficient, with the appropriate sign.

A second-order test captures only the first two possible coefficients. Even tests at arbitrarily high finite order concern behavior near the given configuration.

Semialgebraic curve selection permits an exact description of local descent in terms of convergent Puiseux arcs. Absence of such arcs characterizes local minimality. But Theorem 4 supplies configurations where no local descent arc exists, although a distant packing has strictly smaller diameter.

This is the precise obstruction to promoting complete local optimality into global optimality.

## 8. Exact-contact implications and the remaining obstruction

The stronger sector theorem establishes a genuinely quantitative distribution property of the original extreme sites. It rules out an optimal hull whose vertices become sparse on any fixed positive-angle arc.

Nevertheless, it gives no exact unit triangle.

The reason is structural: (1), the Steiner annulus, support energy, cap deficit, and the quantization estimate are all continuous geometric measurements. Exact unit contacts are an equality phenomenon.

An arbitrarily small anisotropic stretch of a unit-separated packing can eliminate all unit equilateral triangles while increasing diameter arbitrarily little. Such a stretched configuration can retain essentially the same area deficit, hull-vertex distribution, and angular-sector estimates. The theorem therefore does not distinguish exact endpoint rigidity from configurations merely close to the endpoint.

In particular, there is no justified deduction here of a strict diameter reduction for every triangle-free packing, nor a proof that three original sites have pairwise distances exactly one.

The project would still need an all-label global optimality argument: either a rigidity theorem forcing an exact triangular contact at the minimum diameter, or an infinite construction accompanied by a valid lower bound against every competing configuration with the same number of original sites.

A unit-rhombic quadrilateral already illustrates this: its four perimeter edges are unit contacts, its diagonals are strictly greater than one for angles between 60∘60^\circ60∘ and 90∘90^\circ90∘, and the two non-diametral vertices are each constrained by two independent contacts to the opposite diametral endpoints. Second, global maximality of JJJ does not transfer automatically to an arbitrary triangle-free optimizer. The set of triangle-free global minimizers need not be closed. ## 7. Implications for the large-nnn research program

The eight-point obstruction rules out a universal contact-representative theorem. It does not automatically persist for arbitrarily large nnn.

In particular, one cannot infer from the n=8n=8n=8 example that

Tn≠∅⟹no triangle-free representative has degree ≥2\mathcal T_n\ne\varnothing \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \text{no triangle-free representative has degree }\ge2Tn​=∅⟹no triangle-free representative has degree ≥2

for infinitely many nnn.

The exact eight-point example also explains why a local contact-augmentation algorithm can fail. A strictly interior site with one unit neighbor can lie on an admissible arc whose endpoints create exact equilateral triangles. Maximizing contact count while remaining triangle-free may leave that site with only one neighbor.

The established global-density and geometric estimates supplied in the assignment, including the Oler bound, translated-lattice competition, hull-vertex lower bounds, six-neighbor near-hexagon estimates and disk-union charge estimates, do not currently eliminate this exact obstruction.

Their implications concern bulk density, hull geometry or approximate local regularity. The eight-point calculation concerns a discrete transition of exact contact equalities.

To turn the conditional local JJJ-maximality lemma into an eventual theorem, an additional large-nnn argument would need to establish at least one of the following: existence of a triangle-free local JJJ-maximizer among global minimizers, or an alternative selection principle that rules out triangle-blocked interior sites. Neither statement follows from the supplied estimates.

There is also no legitimate route through a positive uniform triangle-free diameter gap. For a finite optimal configuration, a sufficiently small generic anisotropic deformation, followed by normalization to minimum separation 1, can eliminate all unit triangles while making the diameter arbitrarily close to optimal. Exact global optimality is therefore essential.
